snippet: Taiwan's Ministry of Environment (MOENV) will establish an urban forestry smart governance demonstration site around National Taipei University of Technology and the cultural site at the former Air Force Command Headquarters, using digital twin technology to simulate shade and cooling. title: China's auto supply chain shifts from price wars to value competition
snippet: China's cooling auto price war is creating an opportunity for the automotive supply chain to upgrade, as regulators tighten oversight of the new energy vehicle (NEV) industry and curb malicious price cuts. Automakers are being pushed to compete through technological improvements and service quality rather than aggressive discounting, easing margin pressure on parts suppliers.

title: SenseCore captures nearly half of China's neocloud market as heterogeneous chips boost compute efficiency

title: Samsung targets physical AI as Lee Jae-yong leads robotics push

As Samsung integrates its research organizations and plans manufacturing-floor applications, robotics is emerging as a key pillar of its physical AI strategy.

title: LGD invests in Guangzhou for world's first 111-inch OLED line
snippet: LG Display (LGD) is increasing its investment to upgrade its OLED plant in Guangzhou, China, with plans to build the world's first dedicated 111-inch OLED module production line. The move targets the premium TV and commercial display markets, expanding customers' choices with ultra-large displays and strengthening LGD's product competitiveness.

title: Nvidia trims HBM4 bandwidth for Rubin platform, sources say
snippet: Nvidia is reportedly adjusting the fourth-generation high-bandwidth memory (HBM4) specification for its Vera Rubin NVL72 platform, cutting bandwidth per GPU from the previously announced 22TB/s to 19.2TB/s, a reduction of about 13%. South Korean industry observers said the move could increase supply flexibility and help balance performance with mass-production delivery, although the reason for the change and its actual impact on supplier orders remain unconfirmed.
